# dsh-terminal-theme
English | 中文
Color themes for the DeepSeek Harness terminal panel: choose a built-in palette, or import your own
from JSON. The colors apply to the terminal only — the rest of DSH keeps the active theme.
## Features
- **Terminal-only colors.** Every rule is scoped to the terminal panel, so the sidebar, the conversa

tion, and Settings still read the DSH theme tokens.
- **Independent of light and dark.** A terminal

theme keeps its colors when the application switches scheme.
- **Importable palettes.** Paste JSON o

r load a `.json` file; themes are validated, normalized, and stored in the browser.
- **Fully revers
ible.** Pick "Follow app theme" and the terminal returns to the stock DSH appearance; nothing else i
ck "Follow app theme" and the terminal returns to the stock DSH appearance; nothing else is touched.
## Install
The native **Plugins** page installs it: **Add plugin** → paste a spec → **Install**. Three specs wo
native **Plugins** page installs it: **Add plugin** → paste a spec → **Install**. Three specs work:
| Spec | When to use |

| `dsh-terminal-theme` | Once the package is published to npm |
| `https://github.com/wnanbei/dsh-te

rminal-theme` | Straight from GitHub; pnpm clones the repository, and there is no build step |
| `/U
sers/wnanbei/code/dsh-terminal-theme` | From a local clone you keep editing (installs a `link:` depe
bei/code/dsh-terminal-theme` | From a local clone you keep editing (installs a `link:` dependency) |
The dialog also takes a tarball, a `git+https://…` address, and a different registry for that one in
stall. It refuses a package that declares no bundle patch, so the repository root must stay a comple
efuses a package that declares no bundle patch, so the repository root must stay a complete package.
A local-directory install links the folder into the active profile (`~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/node_
modules/dsh-terminal-theme`), so later edits in that clone take effect on the next page reload witho
ut repacking. A GitHub install copies the package into the profile instead, so updating means removi
ng and re-adding it. Either way an existing installation is reported as already installed — remove t
he bundle first to switch sources.

> Agents use the same operation: `plugin_manager` `install_bundle` with one of these specs.
## Usage

1. Open the terminal panel in the right sidebar, then go to **Settings → Terminal colors**.
2. Pick

a card under **Color themes**; the terminal repaints immediately.
3. Pick **Follow app theme** to re
store the default, including the light/dark switch.
Importing a theme:
- Paste JSON into **Import a theme** and press **Import and apply**, or press **Import from file** t

o load a `.json` file.
- **Fill template** writes a complete, directly editable example.
- **Copy cu

rrent theme** exports the active palette; rename it and import it back to create a variant.
- The `×
` on a custom theme card deletes it.
Themes live in the browser (`localStorage`), not in the profile configuration, so they survive DSH u
pgrades and stay out of other browsers.
## Theme JSON format
[代码示例省略，未执行]
| Field | Required | Description |

| `name` | yes | Display name, 1–60 characters |
| `background` / `foreground` | yes | Terminal back

ground and default text color |
| `cursor` | no | Cursor color; defaults to `foreground` |
| `select

ion` | no | Selection fill; defaults to `foreground` at 30% |
| `ansi` | yes | 16 colors: black, red
, green, yellow, blue, magenta, cyan, white, then the 8 bright variants. 8 colors are accepted too a

nd reused for the bright half |
| `extended` | no | Up to 240 colors for indexes 16–255 of the 256-c

the bright half |
| `extended` | no | Up to 240 colors for indexes 16–255 of the 256-color palette |
Colors must be hexadecimal (`#rgb` or `#rrggbb`, normalized to lowercase `#rrggbb`); anything else i
s rejected on import with the reason shown on the page.
## How it works
- All rules are scoped to the `[data-sidebar-terminal]` subtree: `--dsw-alias-bg-base` and `--dsw-al
ias-label-primary` are rebound there, and the xterm DOM renderer's `.xterm-fg-N` / `.xterm-bg-N` rul

es are overridden. No global DSH theme token changes.
- The plugin neither replaces nor wraps the te
rminal component, and never reads or writes its private state. Deselecting a theme only removes the

injected stylesheet.
- The terminal's own OSC color handling, contrast adjustment, and cursor visibi

lity logic keep working as before.
- Another built-in theme needs one entry in `BUILTINS` in `client
.js`; anything else can go through the Settings page.
## Built-in themes

## Development
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Reload the page after editing `client.js`: the plugin manager's install record points at this direct
ory, so no reinstall is needed.
## Releasing
Versions follow Semantic Versioning: a **major** bump when the theme JSON schema or an existing buil
t-in id changes incompatibly, a **minor** bump for new palettes or Settings features, a **patch** bu
es incompatibly, a **minor** bump for new palettes or Settings features, a **patch** bump for fixes.
`version` in `package.json` is the only source of truth, and the tag is `v<version>`:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Pushing the tag runs `.github/workflows/release.yml`, which refuses a tag that disagrees with `packa
ge.json`, re-runs the checks, packs the plugin, and publishes a GitHub Release named after the tag —
with the `.tgz` attached and notes generated from the commits since the previous tag.
The tarball is an install spec too, so a release can be pinned without npm:
- `https://github.com/wnanbei/dsh-terminal-theme/releases/download/v1.2.0/dsh-terminal-theme-1.2.0.t

gz` pins that release
- `https://github.com/wnanbei/dsh-terminal-theme` tracks the default branch
Every push to `main` runs `.github/workflows/verify.yml`, which is the same `node scripts/check.mjs`
very push to `main` runs `.github/workflows/verify.yml`, which is the same `node scripts/check.mjs`.
